mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate at or below 0.05% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced cost of capital.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.05%.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) over the prior month indicate weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising for 3 months) increase cost of capital, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth rate > 2.0%) signals robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through elevated corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 90.0 in the prior month signals manufacturing slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced corporate output.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 90.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth (PAYEMS growth rate < 0.1% monthly) and rising unemployment (UNRATE increase > 0.1pp) signal labor market stress, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS growth rate < 0.1% and UNRATE increases > 0.1pp.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion (CPIAUCSL inflation rate > 3.0% and HOUST housing starts declining for 2 months) signals economic peak, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced growth momentum.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and HOUST declines for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and HOUST declines for 2 months.
